If it is found that we need to pre-read some blocks before a write
can succeed
column2: we normally set STRIPE_DELAYED and don't actually perform

column1: the read until STRIPE_PREREAD_ACTIVE subsequently gets set.
However for a degraded RAID6 we currently perform the reads as soon
as we see that a write is pending.  This significantly hurts
throughput.
So:
- when handle_stripe_dirtying find a block that it wants on a device
that is failed
- when fetch_block detects that a read might be required to satisfy a
write
column2: only perform the read if STRIPE_PREREAD_ACTIVE is set

column1: and if we would actually need to read something to complete the write.
This also helps RAID5
column2: though less often as RAID5 supports a

column1: read-modify-write cycle.  For RAID5 the read is performed too early
only if the write is not a full 4K aligned write (i.e. no an
R5_OVERWRITE).
Also clean up a couple of horrible bits of formatting.
